page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor configured with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs. System memory totals 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports Advanced Vector Extensions up to AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography features such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance provides 3 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes zero local storage, requiring block storage attachment for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects moderate single-thread execution paired with limited multi-core and memory scaling. Single-core performance falls in average ranges, demonstrated by a stress-ng score of 1876.59 and a Geekbench single-core result of 1566.0. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks show lower throughput, registering 3865.79 in stress-ng and 3365.0 in Geekbench. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth measure 31.76 GB/sec and 25.49 GB/sec respectively, placing memory subsystem performance in lower comparative tiers. Test results for software compilation, static web serving, and database operations similarly fall into bottom-quartile performance metrics.

The ecs.c7.xlarge configuration offers a entry-level dedicated resource footprint for workloads where heavy memory bandwidth and multi-core parallel processing are not primary constraints. Its support for vector instructions provides predictable efficiency for basic vector computations, single-threaded tasks, small-model text generation, and lightweight microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. It features 2 physical cores, 4 dedicated vCPUs, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage attached. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 and AES cryptography. Synthetic benchmarks show average single-core performance, evidenced by a 1566.0 Geekbench single-core score, but multi-core operations and memory bandwidth remain in lower performance tiers. The 2.0 GB memory per vCPU allocation creates throughput bottlenecks under parallel multi-threaded loads or memory-dense applications. This instance is best suited for entry-level light compute workloads, single-threaded text processing, basic web serving, and lightweight microservices requiring dedicated hardware allocation.
